title: Offline maps & route planning
label: OFFLINE INFORMATION
deck: Save maps before service fails, write down your destination and at least one alternative, and check the actual route against current hazards. An offline map does not show live closures, fighting, damaged bridges or flooding. GPS position may still work without data, but accuracy and battery life are not guaranteed.

steps: Use the map app’s offline feature for the whole journey, not just the destination. Test it with mobile data off.
Write addresses, landmarks, route choices and emergency contacts. Carry a paper map if available.
Consider flood zones, damaged structures, access needs and transport restrictions. The fastest app route is not necessarily the safest.
Reduce unnecessary screen use and keep a power bank available. Know how to view the downloaded map without needing a new connection.
Stop in a safe place to compare the route with visible conditions and recent trusted reports. Do not enter an uncertain road simply because the map displays it.

decisions: First decision: Download before the outage

Use the map app’s offline feature for the whole journey, not just the destination. Test it with mobile data off. Decide which person can carry this out immediately and what would prevent it in your current location. Do not delay the protective step to complete a household worksheet.

Use known routes and written landmarks while checking conditions from safe positions. If you cannot identify a safe onward route, reassess rather than consuming the last battery on repeated rerouting. Reassess the next available location or resource using the warning signs in this guide; do not assume a promised service is operating.

Maps and position tools are aids, not proof of safe passage. Avoid unfamiliar shortcuts through hazardous or recently fought-over ground. Check the actual route and the needs of the person who will have the most difficulty moving. A destination is not confirmed until access and conditions have been checked.

sections: Check the route from both ends

Study the approach to the destination as well as the route out. Record recognizable junctions, alternate access and where the household will meet if a pickup point becomes unreachable. Test downloaded map coverage before a trip rather than assuming the overview map includes every street. Keep written addresses separate from the phone; avoid posting a private destination in a public message.
